entities.name: calorimetry
entities.definition: Calorimetry describes the experimental technique for measuring heat transfer during chemical or physical changes. This method relies on observing temperature variations within an insulated system to calculate energy exchange values accurately.

entities.name: adaptive optics
entities.definition: Adaptive optics are advanced systems integrated into telescopes to correct image distortions caused by Earth's atmosphere. By rapidly adjusting mirror shapes in response to atmospheric turbulence, these technologies restore sharpness and significantly improve the resolution of astronomical observations.

entities.name: unit testing
entities.definition: A development practice that exercises the smallest testable pieces of a program in isolation, usually individual functions or methods, against expected outcomes. Automated unit suites run quickly, localize defects, and support safe refactoring, though they do not replace integration or end-to-end tests.

entities.name: version control
entities.definition: Version control is a systematic method for tracking changes to project files over time and managing multiple iterations simultaneously. entities.name: addition method
entities.definition: The addition method is a systematic algebraic technique for solving systems of linear equations. It involves adding modified versions of the original equations to eliminate one variable, thereby simplifying the system so that substitution can determine all unknowns.
